meta.title: Solemtrix — vineyard inventory from drone imagery, for public institutions
meta.description: The complete map of a municipality's vineyards: blocks, rows, every plant, gaps and waste, measured from drone imagery with AI, plus field inspection tasks with a route. Free pilot for municipalities.

hero.eyebrow: For municipalities, district councils and agricultural agencies
hero.title: Every vineyard in the commune, measured row by row
hero.subtitle: Solemtrix turns drone imagery into the complete map of the plantations: blocks, rows, every plant, gaps and waste. And the team gets inspection tasks with a ready-to-walk route.
hero.imageAlt: Solemtrix map: vineyard block V12 in Sireți, with AI-detected rows over the orthophoto and the block's card

problem.title: Vineyard data no longer keeps up with the field
problem.subtitle: Decisions on subsidies, abandoned land and registers rely on self-declarations and on rare, costly manual checks.

items.title: The register and the statistics disagree
items.text: The Vine and Wine Register and the National Bureau of Statistics reported wine-grape areas more than 20,000 ha apart (2024). The register relies on self-declarations.

items.title: More is uprooted than planted
items.text: For every hectare planted in the last 8 years, seven were uprooted. Records change faster than they can be checked in the field.

items.title: Subsidy control without an integrated system
items.text: The Land Parcel Identification System (LPIS) was piloted in only five districts. The Court of Accounts points to missing traceability and a risk of double funding.

items.title: Abandoned land is checked on complaint
items.text: Land Code no. 22/2024 lets the municipality lease out land left uncultivated for 2 years, but the finding is made in the field, case by case.

how.title: How it works
how.subtitle: From a drone flight to a list of field checks, in four steps.

steps.title: Drone flight
steps.text: A licensed operator photographs the commune at 2.5 cm/px. The result: an orthophoto where every vine is visible.

steps.title: AI analysis
steps.text: The model detects blocks, rows, each plant's canopy, inter-rows, gaps and waste. A human operator can correct the annotations before publishing.

steps.title: The municipality's map
steps.text: Each municipality sees only the area within its administrative boundary: map, indicators per block and row, tables and export.

steps.title: Field tasks
steps.text: Gaps, missing plants and waste become tasks for inspectors, with a due date, priority, notification and an optimised route (GPX for the phone).

items.title: Every row, with length, plants and the largest gap
items.text: Click any row or block: length, number of plants, largest gap, canopy and inter-row area. Search by code, measure distances and areas, 3D view.
items.alt: Row V12-R003 on the map, marked disrupted, with a largest gap of 46.7 m

items.title: From the AI analysis straight to the inspector's list
items.text: The municipality admin picks the targets and assigns them to the team with a due date and priority. The inspector is notified, sees the place on the map and closes the task with a field note.
items.alt: The Field tasks page with AI targets ready to assign

items.title: Works on a phone
items.text: The map, the tasks and the route open on the inspector's phone. The route exports to GPX for any navigation app.
items.alt: The Solemtrix map on a phone, with a row selected

items.title: Figures ready for a report
items.text: The municipality dashboard gathers areas, the number of blocks, rows and plants, disrupted rows and the route. Tables export to CSV in the organisers' format.
items.alt: The Sireți municipality dashboard with the plantation indicators

security.title: Security and data
security.subtitle: Built for public data, with strict rules on who sees what.

items.title: Hosted in the European Union
items.text: The database runs in the Ireland data centre. Encryption in transit and at rest is provided by the infrastructure provider.

items.title: Each municipality sees only its data
items.text: Isolation per municipality is enforced by the database (row-level policies), not only by the interface.

items.title: Clear roles
items.text: Municipality admin, inspector, viewer. Nobody sets someone else's password: members are invited by email.

items.title: Action log
items.text: Enrolments, accounts and access changes are recorded in a log that cannot be edited.

items.title: The data belongs to the institution
items.text: Export at any time in open formats: CSV, GPX, GeoJSON.

items.title: In the state language
items.text: Interface in Romanian, with English and Russian for mixed teams.

security.note: Personal data is processed under Law no. 195/2024 on personal data protection; the terms are agreed in writing with each institution before the pilot.

engagement.title: How we start
engagement.subtitle: No procurement at first: the pilot runs under a cooperation agreement.

steps.title: Free pilot
steps.text: One commune, one flight, the map and tasks for the municipality's team. At the end: a report and a decision.

steps.title: Subscription per municipality
steps.text: Priced by vineyard area, sized for the low-value procurement procedure. Flights are quoted separately.

steps.title: Project at scale
steps.text: For district councils and central agencies: a contract via MTender, possibly co-funded by European programmes.

engagement.budgetNote: The local budget for next year is approved by 10 December: autumn is the right time to include the subscription.

items.a: A drone operator licensed under Government Decision no. 949/2022. We organise the flight together with the municipality; within 10 km of the border the Border Police's approval is also required.

items.q: Do the measurements have legal value?
items.a: They do not replace the cadastre or property titles. They are working data that show precisely where a field check is worth it and how much area is planted.

items.q: Why a drone and not a satellite?
items.a: They complement each other. Free satellite imagery has 10 m per pixel and shows the parcel; the drone has 2.5 cm per pixel and shows every plant, the gaps in a row and the waste.

items.q: What does the municipality need to provide?
items.a: A contact person and consent for the flight. We take the commune's administrative boundary from OpenStreetMap, and the municipality admin creates the team's accounts.

items.q: Where is the data and who owns it?
items.a: In the European Union (Ireland). The data belongs to the institution, which can export it at any time in open formats.

Areas and lengths are computed in metres, planimetrically, from 2.5 cm/px imagery. AI annotations can be checked and corrected by a human operator before publishing, and any row can be checked on the orthophoto.
The pilot requires no procurement. The yearly subscription can be bought through the low-value procurement procedure; large projects through MTender.
